examples.ko: 노후를 편안하게 영위하려면 미리 준비해야 해요.
examples.en: If you want to live your later years comfortably, you have to prepare in advance.

examples.ko: 그분은 시골에서 소박한 삶을 영위하고 있어요.
examples.en: He lives a simple life in the countryside.

examples.ko: 누구나 인간다운 생활을 영위할 수 있어야 해요.
examples.en: Everyone should be able to lead a decent life.

examples.ko: 이 마을 사람들은 농사를 지으며 생계를 영위해요.
examples.en: The people in this village make a living by farming.

examples.ko: 은퇴 후에도 활기찬 일상을 영위하는 분이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people lead an active daily life even after retiring.

examples.ko: 가난 때문에 평범한 삶을 영위하기 어려웠어요.
examples.en: Because of poverty, it was hard to lead an ordinary life.

explain: '살다'보다 격식 있는 글말이라 뉴스나 글에서 많이 나와요. '삶, 생활, 생계, 일상'처럼 사는 방식을 나타내는 말과 같이 써요. 말할 때는 보통 '살다'나 '꾸려 가다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is a more formal, written-style word than '살다' (to live), so it shows up often in news and writing. It pairs with words for a way of living, such as 삶, 생활, 생계 and 일상. In casual speech people usually say '살다' or '꾸려 가다'.

examples.ko: 그 광고는 소비자를 오도할 수 있어요.
examples.en: That advertisement can mislead consumers.
Wrong statistics mislead people's judgment.

examples.ko: 기사 제목이 독자를 오도하지 않게 신경 써야 해요.
examples.en: You have to be careful that the headline doesn't mislead readers.
I had no intention of deliberately misleading anyone about the facts.

examples.ko: 이 설명은 학생들을 오도했다는 비판을 받았어요.
examples.en: This explanation was criticized for misleading students.
Exaggerated expressions sometimes mislead public opinion.

explain: '속이다'는 일부러 거짓을 말하는 느낌이 강하지만, '오도하다'는 사람을 잘못된 방향으로 이끈다는 느낌이라 의도가 없어도 쓸 수 있어요. '여론, 독자, 소비자, 판단' 같은 말과 자주 쓰고 뉴스나 글에서 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '잘못 알게 하다'처럼 쉽게 말해요.
explain_en: '속이다' (to deceive) usually suggests a deliberate lie, while '오도하다' means leading people in a wrong direction, so it can be used even without bad intent. It often goes with 여론, 독자, 소비자 and 판단, and appears mostly in news and writing. In daily conversation people say something easier like '잘못 알게 하다'.

examples.en: Buddhism believes in reincarnation.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 윤회 사상을 바탕으로 만들었어요.
examples.en: This movie is based on the idea of reincarnation.

examples.ko: 죽으면 다시 태어난다는 윤회 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard the story of reincarnation, that you are born again after death.
My grandmother seriously believes in reincarnation.

examples.ko: 소설 속 주인공은 윤회를 거듭하며 사랑을 찾아요.
examples.en: The hero of the novel goes through repeated reincarnations in search of love.

examples.ko: 윤회에서 벗어나는 것이 불교의 목표라고 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned that escaping reincarnation is the goal of Buddhism.

explain: '환생'은 다시 태어나는 일을 말할 때 드라마나 영화에서 많이 쓰고, '윤회'는 태어나고 죽는 일이 계속 돌고 도는 불교의 생각을 말할 때 써요. '윤회 사상', '윤회를 믿다', '윤회에서 벗어나다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: '환생' is common in dramas and movies for being born again, while '윤회' refers to the Buddhist idea of birth and death repeating in a cycle. Common patterns are 윤회 사상, 윤회를 믿다 and 윤회에서 벗어나다.

examples.en: Bats find their way using sound waves.
Sound waves travel far even underwater.

examples.ko: 이 기계는 음파로 물고기 떼를 찾아내요.
examples.en: This machine finds schools of fish using sound waves.

examples.ko: 소리는 음파가 되어 공기를 타고 전달돼요.
examples.en: Sound becomes sound waves and travels through the air.

examples.ko: 음파의 진동이 약해서 소리가 잘 안 들려요.
examples.en: The vibration of the sound waves is weak, so I can't hear well.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 음파를 그림으로 그려 봤어요.
examples.en: In science class we drew sound waves as pictures.

explain: 소리가 퍼져 나가는 파동을 말해서 과학 수업이나 설명에서 많이 나와요. 사람이 못 듣는 높은 소리는 '초음파'라고 하고, 병원 검사에서도 들을 수 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '소리'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means the wave by which sound spreads, so it comes up mostly in science classes and explanations. Sound too high for people to hear is called '초음파' (ultrasound), which you also hear about in hospital exams. In everyday talk people simply say '소리'.

en: book someone for; book someone on a charge

examples.en: The police have booked the driver and are investigating.
They booked the owner who operated without a license.

examples.ko: 경찰이 그 사람을 입건할지 아직 정하지 못했어요.
examples.en: The police haven't decided yet whether to book that person.

examples.ko: 사기 혐의로 입건하기 전에 먼저 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: They heard his side first before booking him on a fraud charge.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 경찰이 세 명을 입건했다고 해요.
examples.en: The news says the police booked three people.

examples.ko: 단속에 걸린 사람들을 모두 입건하지는 않았어요.
examples.en: They did not book everyone caught in the crackdown.

explain: 경찰이 어떤 사람을 정식 수사 대상으로 올린다는 뜻이라서 '체포하다, 구속하다'처럼 몸을 붙잡아 두는 것과는 달라요. 주로 뉴스나 경찰 이야기에서 나오고 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 써요. '입건되다'로도 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It means the police formally register someone as a subject of investigation, which is different from '체포하다' (arrest) or '구속하다' (detain), where the person is physically held. It appears mainly in news and police reports and is rarely used in daily talk. You will also often see the passive form '입건되다'.

examples.en: Our country has a long history.

examples.ko: 이 바위는 장구한 세월 동안 바람을 맞았어요.
examples.en: This rock has been exposed to the wind for a very long time.
That tradition has continued for a very long time.
Since the history is long, there is a lot to see.
This temple's history is truly long.
The long-running debate finally ended.

explain: '길다'와 달리 시간, 역사, 세월처럼 오랜 기간에만 쓰는 글말이에요. '장구한 역사', '장구한 세월'처럼 앞에서 꾸며 주는 꼴로 가장 많이 써요. 악기 '장구'와는 소리만 같고 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: Unlike '길다' (long), it is a written-style word used only for long spans of time, such as history and years. It is most often used before a noun, as in '장구한 역사' and '장구한 세월'. It sounds the same as the drum '장구' but is a different word.

examples.ko: 경찰은 제보자의 이름을 비밀로 해 줬어요.
examples.en: The police kept the tipster's name secret.

examples.ko: 제보자가 알려 준 장소에 가 봤어요.
examples.en: I went to the place the tipster told us about.
The broadcasting station contacted the tipster.
Thanks to an anonymous tipster, the problem became known.

examples.ko: 이 소식의 제보자는 같은 동네 사람이었어요.
examples.en: The source of this news was someone from the same neighborhood.
There is a law that protects whistleblowers.

explain: 방송이나 신문, 기관에 정보를 알려 주는 사람을 말해요. '신고자'는 경찰이나 관청에 알리는 사람일 때 많이 쓰고, 제보자는 언론에 알리는 경우에도 자주 써요. '익명의 제보자', '공익 제보자'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a person who gives information to a broadcaster, newspaper or organization. '신고자' is used more for someone reporting to the police or authorities, while 제보자 is also common for tips to the media. Typical phrases are '익명의 제보자' (anonymous tipster) and '공익 제보자' (whistleblower).

examples.en: Don't butt into other people's business so much.

examples.ko: 엄마가 제 옷차림까지 참견해서 조금 힘들어요.
examples.en: It's a bit hard because my mom even interferes with what I wear.

examples.ko: 옆에서 자꾸 참견하면 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: If you keep butting in beside me, I can't concentrate.

examples.ko: 제가 참견할 일은 아니지만 걱정이 돼서요.
examples.en: It's not my place to interfere, but I'm worried.
My younger sibling likes to meddle in her older sister's affairs.

examples.ko: 누가 참견해도 저는 제 길을 갈 거예요.
examples.en: Even if someone interferes, I'll go my own way.

explain: '간섭하다'와 비슷하지만 '참견하다'는 일상 대화에서 많이 쓰고, 달갑지 않게 끼어드는 느낌이 있어요. '남의 일에 참견하다'처럼 '에'와 같이 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 사람에게는 '오지랖이 넓다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '간섭하다' (to interfere), but '참견하다' is more common in everyday talk and carries a feeling of unwelcome butting in. It is often used with the particle '에', as in '남의 일에 참견하다'. For a person like this, Koreans also say '오지랖이 넓다'.

examples.ko: 그 선수의 처절한 노력이 마음에 남았어요.
examples.en: That player's desperate effort stayed in my heart.
I held on desperately until the very last moment.

examples.ko: 주인공의 외침이 너무 처절해서 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: The hero's cry was so heart-wrenching that I cried.

examples.ko: 처절했던 그 시절을 생각하면 지금도 마음이 아파요.
examples.en: When I think of those harsh days, my heart still aches.
His crying is truly heart-rending.

examples.ko: 그 경기는 처절하다고 할 만큼 치열했어요.
examples.en: The game was so intense you could call it desperate.

explain: '치열하다'는 경쟁이나 싸움이 뜨거운 것이고, '처절하다'는 그 안에 비참하고 절박한 느낌이 더해져요. '노력, 외침, 울음, 싸움' 같은 말과 자주 써요. 말보다는 글이나 이야기 속에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: '치열하다' describes a hot, intense competition or fight, while '처절하다' adds a sense of misery and desperation. It often goes with words like 노력, 외침, 울음 and 싸움. It appears more in writing and stories than in casual speech.

examples.ko: 건물을 지을 때 철근을 먼저 세워요.
examples.en: When building a structure, they set up the rebar first.

examples.ko: 이 벽에는 철근이 많이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: There is a lot of rebar in this wall.
They built a sturdy bridge with rebar and concrete.
The price of rebar went up, so the construction cost went up too.
A truck loaded with rebar came into the construction site.

examples.ko: 한옥은 철근 대신 두꺼운 목재 기둥으로 지붕을 받쳐요.
examples.en: A hanok supports its roof with thick wooden pillars instead of rebar.

explain: 콘크리트 안에 넣는 가늘고 긴 쇠막대예요. '철근 콘크리트'라는 짝말로 많이 나오고, 건물의 뼈대로 쓰는 '철골'과는 달라요. 건설이나 뉴스에서 자주 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is the long, thin steel bar placed inside concrete. It appears often in the pair '철근 콘크리트' (reinforced concrete) and is different from '철골', the steel frame of a building. You hear it often in construction talk and the news.

examples.ko: 지구는 태양 주위를 타원 모양으로 돌아요.
examples.en: The Earth goes around the sun in an elliptical shape.

examples.ko: 타원을 그리는 방법을 수학 시간에 배웠어요.
examples.en: We learned how to draw an ellipse in math class.
This table is oval, so it has no corners.
An egg seen from the side is close to an oval.
The oval mirror suits the room well.
The outline of the track is an elongated oval.

explain: 동그란 '원'이 한쪽으로 길쭉해진 모양이에요. 일상에서는 '타원형'이라고 많이 하고, 수학에서는 도형 이름으로 써요. 달걀 같은 모양은 '달걀형'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is the shape of a round '원' (circle) stretched out to one side. In daily life people often say '타원형', and in math it is the name of the figure. An egg-like shape can also be called '달걀형'.

examples.ko: 심판의 편파 판정에 팬들이 화가 났어요.
examples.en: Fans were angry about the referee's biased call.

examples.ko: 이 신문은 편파 보도를 한다는 말을 들어요.
examples.en: People say this newspaper reports in a biased way.
The teacher tries not to act with bias.
That broadcast was criticized as biased.
As the controversy over bias grew, the association apologized.

examples.ko: 한쪽 말만 들으면 편파가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you only listen to one side, it can become bias.

explain: '공정하다'의 반대 느낌이고, '편파 판정', '편파 보도'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 사람이나 태도를 말할 때는 '편파적이다'로 써요. 가족이나 친구를 더 좋아하는 '편애'와는 달라요.
explain_en: It feels like the opposite of '공정하다' (fair) and is often placed before another noun, as in '편파 판정' (biased call) and '편파 보도' (biased reporting). To describe a person or attitude, use '편파적이다'. It differs from '편애', which means favoring someone you like more.

examples.en: The lawmakers vote on the bill this afternoon.
Opinions were divided, so we decided to put it to a vote.

examples.ko: 반장을 뽑을 때 손을 들어 표결했어요.
examples.en: When choosing the class president, we voted by raising hands.
To hold a vote, you first have to decide the agenda item.

examples.ko: 이 안건은 다음 주에 표결할 예정이에요.
examples.en: This item is scheduled to be voted on next week.
Sometimes they decide by applause without voting.

explain: '투표하다'는 선거나 여럿이 고를 때 널리 쓰고, '표결하다'는 회의나 국회에서 안건을 찬성과 반대로 결정할 때 써요. 뉴스에서는 '표결에 부치다', '표결 처리'처럼 명사 '표결'로도 많이 나와요.
explain_en: '투표하다' is used widely for elections or any group choice, while '표결하다' is for deciding an agenda item by yes or no votes in a meeting or the National Assembly. In the news the noun '표결' is also common, as in '표결에 부치다' and '표결 처리'.

en: determination to win; certainty of victory

examples.en: I'll present our team's winning strategy.
The players entered the stadium determined to win.

examples.ko: 경기 전에 모두 필승! 하고 외쳤어요.
examples.en: Before the game, everyone shouted 'Victory!'
Their will to win this match is tremendous.
We are saving our trump card.
The players, vowing to win, had bright expressions.

explain: '반드시 이긴다'는 뜻으로 '필승 전략', '필승 각오', '필승 의지', '필승 카드'처럼 다른 말 앞에서 많이 써요. 응원 구호로 '필승!'이라고 외치기도 해요. 반대로 '반드시 진다'는 말은 '필패'라고 해요.
explain_en: It carries the sense of 'certain to win' and is often placed before other nouns, as in 필승 전략, 필승 각오, 필승 의지 and 필승 카드. People also shout '필승!' as a cheer. The opposite, 'certain to lose', is '필패'.

examples.en: A lecture event is being held at the library this weekend.
I went to a famous author's lecture.

examples.ko: 강연회는 무료이니까 누구나 올 수 있어요.
examples.en: The lecture is free, so anyone can come.
I was busy last week preparing for the lecture event.
The lecture hall was full of people.
I heard the date of next month's lecture has changed.

explain: '강연'은 사람 앞에서 말하는 일이고, '강연회'는 그런 이야기를 듣는 모임이에요. 학교 수업 안에서 하는 특별한 강의는 '특강'이라고 많이 해요. 장소는 '강연회장'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '강연' is the act of giving a talk in front of people, and '강연회' is the event where you listen to such a talk. A special lecture within school classes is often called '특강'. The venue is called '강연회장'.

examples.ko: 이 드라마는 옛 복장을 꼼꼼히 고증했어요.
examples.en: This drama carefully researched the period costumes.

examples.ko: 역사학자들이 당시 생활 모습을 고증하고 있어요.
examples.en: Historians are verifying how people lived at the time.
It's a scene made without historical research, so it feels awkward.

examples.ko: 옛 문서를 보고 건물의 위치를 고증할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can determine the building's location by looking at old documents.

examples.ko: 사극을 만들 때는 시대를 고증해야 해요.
examples.en: When making a historical drama, you have to research the era.

examples.ko: 전문가가 고증해 준 덕분에 소품이 정확해요.
examples.en: Thanks to the expert's research, the props are accurate.

explain: 옛 문헌이나 유물을 근거로 사실을 밝힌다는 느낌이라서 단순히 '조사하다'보다 역사적인 근거가 중요해요. 요즘은 드라마와 영화에서 '고증이 잘됐다', '고증 오류'처럼 명사로 더 많이 들려요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of establishing facts from old documents or relics, so historical evidence matters more than in a plain '조사하다' (to investigate). Today you hear it more as a noun in dramas and films, as in '고증이 잘됐다' and '고증 오류'.

examples.en: The new shoes have a sparkling shine.
It's a fabric with a subtle sheen, so it looks luxurious.

examples.ko: 오래 써서 가죽 가방의 광택은 많이 사라졌어요.
examples.en: After long use, the leather bag has lost much of its gloss.

examples.ko: 광택 없는 종이가 눈에 편해서 좋아요.
examples.en: I like matte paper because it's easy on the eyes.

examples.ko: 이 립스틱은 광택도 오래가고 색도 예뻐요.
examples.en: This lipstick keeps its gloss for a long time and the color is pretty too.
The feel of a photo changes depending on the finish.

explain: 물건 표면이 반짝이는 정도를 말하고, '광택이 나다', '광택이 없다'처럼 써요. 머리카락이나 피부가 반짝일 때는 '윤기'를 더 많이 써요. 일상에서는 '윤이 나다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It describes how shiny an object's surface is, as in '광택이 나다' and '광택이 없다'. For shiny hair or skin, '윤기' is more common. In daily speech people also say '윤이 나다'.

examples.en: The idols' group dance was truly perfect.
Migratory birds perform a group dance in the sky.

examples.ko: 열 명이 함께 추는 군무가 멋있었어요.
examples.en: The group dance performed by ten people was cool.

examples.ko: 군무 연습 때문에 매일 늦게까지 남아요.
examples.en: I stay late every day because of group dance practice.
In a ballet ensemble dance, the dancers have to be in sync.
This song is famous for its group choreography.

explain: 여러 사람이 함께 추는 춤을 말하고, 혼자 추는 '독무'의 반대예요. 아이돌 춤이 정확하게 맞으면 '칼군무'라고 많이 말해요. 새 떼나 물고기 떼가 한꺼번에 움직이는 모습을 '군무'에 비유하기도 해요.
explain_en: It means a dance performed by many people together, the opposite of '독무' (a solo dance). When an idol group's moves match precisely, people often say '칼군무'. Flocks of birds or schools of fish moving together are also compared to a 군무.

en: to nod slightly; to move slightly

examples.en: He greeted me with a slight nod.

examples.ko: 너무 피곤해서 손가락 하나 까딱하기 싫어요.
examples.en: I'm so tired I don't want to lift a finger.
One slip and I would have been late.

examples.ko: 아이가 음악에 맞춰 발을 까딱하고 있어요.
examples.en: The child is tapping a foot to the music.

examples.ko: 누가 불러도 그는 까딱하지 않고 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: No matter who called him, he sat there without budging.
One careless move and there'll be trouble, so be careful.

explain: 고개, 손가락, 발을 살짝 움직이는 모습을 말해요. '까딱하면', '까딱하다가는'은 조금만 실수하면 나쁜 일이 생길 것 같다는 뜻으로 많이 써요. 보통 '고개를 까딱하다'처럼 목적어와 같이 써요.

phrases.example: 동생은 집안일에는 손가락 하나 까딱하지 않아요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling doesn't lift a finger to do housework.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금도 일을 하지 않고 가만히 있을 때 쓰는 말이에요. 게으른 사람을 비판하는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone does no work at all and just stays still. It carries a tone of criticizing a lazy person.

explain_en: It describes a slight movement of the head, a finger or a foot. '까딱하면' and '까딱하다가는' are commonly used to mean that one small mistake could bring bad results. It is usually used with an object, as in '고개를 까딱하다'.

examples.en: When politicians make promises left and right, it's hard to believe them.
This shop hands out coupons far too freely.
A way of speaking that overuses foreign words is uncomfortable to hear.
We have to manage things so receipts aren't issued carelessly.
The company made promises recklessly, and the employees got worn out.
I used my credit cards too freely and my debt grew.

explain: 말, 약속, 쿠폰, 공약 등을 함부로 자꾸 내놓는다는 나쁜 느낌이 있어요. '남용하다'는 권한이나 약을 지나치게 쓰는 것이고, '남발하다'는 무언가를 마구 내놓는 것이라 달라요. 피동 표현은 '남발되다'예요.
explain_en: It has a negative feeling of recklessly and repeatedly putting out words, promises, coupons or pledges. '남용하다' is overusing something like authority or medicine, while '남발하다' is handing things out carelessly, so they differ. The passive form is '남발되다'.

examples.en: Our team won big in the final.
Yesterday's game ended in a landslide win for us.
Fans cheered at the news of the big win.
This election was a landslide victory for the ruling party.
A big win looked certain, but they were caught up at the end.

examples.ko: 이렇게 큰 점수 차는 대승이라고 부를 만해요.
examples.en: A score gap this big can be called a landslide.

explain: 점수 차나 결과가 크게 이겼을 때 쓰고, '대승을 거두다'가 가장 자주 나오는 말이에요. 반대로 크게 졌을 때는 '대패'라고 해요. 스포츠나 선거 뉴스에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when a win is by a wide margin, and '대승을 거두다' is the most common pattern. When a team loses badly, the word is '대패'. It appears often in sports and election news.

examples.en: My younger sibling looks at the insect guidebook every day.
I looked up this bird's name in the illustrated guide.

examples.ko: 식물 도감이 있으면 산책이 더 재미있어요.
examples.en: If you have a plant guide, walks are more fun.
The pictures in the guide are as detailed as photos.
I browsed the children's illustrated guide section at the bookstore.
This guidebook has more photos than drawings.

explain: 동물, 식물, 곤충처럼 이름을 그림이나 사진으로 알려 주는 책이에요. '식물 도감', '곤충 도감'처럼 앞에 종류를 붙여 써요. 글 중심의 사전이나 백과사전과 달리 모양을 보고 이름을 찾을 때 좋아요.
explain_en: It is a book that shows names with pictures or photos of animals, plants, insects and so on. The type goes in front, as in '식물 도감' and '곤충 도감'. Unlike text-based dictionaries and encyclopedias, it is handy for finding a name by looking at its appearance.

examples.ko: 이 실험 결과는 기존 이론을 반증해요.
examples.en: This experiment's result disproves the existing theory.

examples.ko: 그 주장을 반증할 자료를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for data that can refute that claim.

examples.ko: 새 연구가 예전 가설을 반증했다고 해요.
examples.en: They say a new study disproved the earlier hypothesis.

examples.ko: 그 말을 반증하려면 확실한 증거가 필요해요.
examples.en: To disprove that statement, you need solid evidence.

examples.ko: 상대 의견을 반증하지 못하면 설득력이 없어요.
examples.en: If you can't refute the other side's opinion, it isn't persuasive.

examples.ko: 과학자들은 서로의 주장을 반증하며 발전해 왔어요.
examples.en: Scientists have advanced by disproving each other's claims.

explain: '반박하다'는 말로 맞서 주장하는 것이고, '반증하다'는 반대되는 증거로 어떤 주장이 틀렸음을 보여 주는 거예요. 반대로 맞다는 것을 보이는 말은 '입증하다, 증명하다'예요. 논문이나 토론에서 주로 쓰고 명사 '반증'도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '반박하다' is arguing back in words, while '반증하다' is showing a claim is wrong by presenting contrary evidence. The opposite, showing something is true, is '입증하다' or '증명하다'. It is used mostly in papers and debates, and the noun '반증' is common too.

examples.en: It's an old house, so we redid the wiring.

examples.ko: 전기 배선이 낡아서 불이 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: The electrical wiring is worn, so a fire could start.
Leave the wiring work to a professional.
I covered the wiring under the desk with an organizer box.
We had it inspected to see if there was a problem with the wiring.

examples.ko: 천장 배선 때문에 전등을 옮기기 어려워요.
examples.en: Because of the ceiling wiring, it's hard to move the light.

explain: '전선'은 선 자체이고, '배선'은 전선을 필요한 곳에 이어 설치한 상태나 그 일을 말해요. '전기 배선', '배선 공사'처럼 집을 고치거나 전자 제품을 말할 때 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 '선 정리'처럼 쉽게 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: '전선' is the wire itself, while '배선' is the wiring as laid out and connected where needed, or the work of doing it. It often appears in 전기 배선 and 배선 공사, when talking about home repairs or electronics. In daily talk people may also say something simpler like '선 정리' (tidying cables).
